output.summary: On-screen evidence covers two scenes. In sc_001 (EP50:E1-E32), Catherine and Father Thomas, in bed, negotiate: she asks for his price, and he demands control of the west territory's tax collection routed through his office, presented as discretion rather than absolution; they agree it will hold 'for as long as' the hearing lasts. In sc_002 (EP50:E33-E40), Agnes walks a manor corridor, looks through a door, and sees the two in an intimate embrace before stumbling away. Uncertainty: the on-screen dialogue names only 'Father Thomas' and 'Catherine'; the shirtless priest in EP50:E36 is not named on screen, so his identity rests on continuity with sc_001. Agnes's role, what she intends to do, and the nature of the 'lethal secret' (EP50:E40) are not shown. The supplied metadata (logline, continuity notes) is not on-screen evidence and was not used for any claim here; it describes unseen events such as a prior episode and a 'political extortion' framing that this episode does not show explicitly.

beats.description: Catherine and Father Thomas lie together in bed; their banter turns to a demand for honesty about their attraction.
Catherine asks for his price; Father Thomas demands control of west territory tax collection routed through his office, and Catherine calls it a fortune rather than absolution.

Catherine accepts the terms with a conditional phrasing ('Unsupervised. In your hands alone.'); Father Thomas agrees the arrangement holds 'for as long as it holds', and Catherine frames it as ending when the hearing does.
The pair draw closer, referencing unused rooms and a taste for more than discretion, and embrace intimately.
Agnes walks the corridor, looks through a door, and sees Catherine and the shirtless priest embracing; she reacts in terror and retreats into the shadows.

revelations.claim: Father Thomas demands control of the west territory's tax collection, routed through his office, in exchange for discretion.
